case-1.objects: A and B are arbitrary types equipped with measurable spaces. The data are a measure μ on A, a kernel R from A to B, and a kernel F from A × B to B. For fixed a, write R(a) for the measure on B given by R and F_a(b) = F(a,b) for the fiber kernel obtained by comap along b ↦ (a,b). The joint measure M = μ ⊗ₘ R integrates first against R(a) in b and then against μ in a. The retained-coordinate kernel is K(a,b) = δ_a ⊗ F(a,b).
case-1.domains: The indices a range over A and the fiber states b over B. R(a) and F(a,b) are measures on B. M is on A × B with the product measurable structure, and K is a kernel from A × B to A × B. Fiber flux tests use measurable U,V ⊆ B, while joint flux tests use arbitrary measurable S,T ⊆ A × B. All flux integrals take values in the extended nonnegative reals.
case-1.quantifiers: Universally quantify the two types, their measurable-space instances, the measure μ and its SFinite instance, and the kernels R,F and their IsSFiniteKernel instances. For any hypothesis hF, its premise holds for μ-almost every a, with every pair of measurable U,V ⊆ B quantified inside the almost-everywhere condition. The conclusion is for every pair of measurable S,T ⊆ A × B, not just measurable rectangles.
case-1.assumptions: Assume SFinite μ and IsSFiniteKernel R and F: μ is a countable sum of finite measures, and each kernel has a countable decomposition as finite kernels. In addition, for μ-almost every a and all measurable U,V ⊆ B, the integral of F(a,b)(V) over b in U against R(a) equals the integral of F(a,b)(U) over b in V against R(a). The comap along the measurable inclusion b ↦ (a,b) makes this an assertion of reversibility for the fiber kernel on B.
case-1.conclusion: K = (Kernel.deterministic Prod.fst measurable_fst) ×ₖ F is reversible with respect to M = μ ⊗ₘ R. Precisely, for all measurable S,T ⊆ A × B, the nonnegative integral of K(x)(T) over x in S against M equals the nonnegative integral of K(x)(S) over x in T against M. Here K(a,b)(T) = F(a,b)({b′ : (a,b′) ∈ T}), since the first coordinate is retained.
case-1.senses: Reversibility here is symmetry of measurable-set flux in the extended nonnegative reals, so equality can include two infinite fluxes. The premise is μ-almost everywhere in a, not pointwise at every a. Neither probability normalization nor Markovness, finite total mass, finite flux, sigma-finiteness, or invariance is asserted. The joint measure uses a potentially a-dependent R(a), and the conclusion does not assert independence of the coordinates.
case-1.constants: No free numerical constants, rates, bounds or time parameters occur. Prod.fst is the first-coordinate projection, and Kernel.deterministic Prod.fst is the unit Dirac measure δ_a at the input's first coordinate. The comap uses the constant map with value a paired with the identity on B; ×ₖ forms the pointwise product of kernels, and ⊗ₘ is measure–kernel comp-product, not a product with an a-independent measure.
